justifications.functional_suitability: Video (Video Streaming Gateway Containers), e-prescriptions (FHIR/National Adapter Containers), AI checker (AI Inference & Audit Proxy) and consent (Consent Enforcement Middleware) are covered. Gaps: the AI service is modeled as external, consent management has no patient UI or store, and clinician licensing is absent.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Adaptive bitrate WebRTC in Video Streaming Gateway, Store-and-Forward Cache Agent, Local Async Event Bus and Rate Limiting middleware help. Gaps: no autoscaling, no capacity or latency targets, no data-access optimization, and synchronous audit logging adds latency.
justifications.compatibility: FHIR Translation Adapter (US) and National E-Prescription Adapter (EU) cover R-08 with concrete modules, and OIDC is used for identity. Gaps: no per-country EU adapters, the Notification service has no relationships, and the FHIR scope is limited to prescriptions.
justifications.usability: Patients and Clinicians are a single undifferentiated person with HTTPS/WebRTC access. Adaptive streaming helps rural users, but there are no client apps, consent management UI, separate clinician or pharmacist interfaces, or accessibility and language provisions.
justifications.reliability: Store-and-Forward Cache Agent, Local Async Event Bus with durable SQLite/RocksDB storage and the Local File Buffer give degraded-mode resilience for R-06. Gaps: no multi-zone failover, health checks, backups or recovery design, and no explicit fallback to audio-only.
justifications.security: ExtAuthz Filter default-deny consent, mTLS, Secret Manager sidecar, KMS encryption, PII/PHI Stripping Filter and AI audit logging of inputs/model version address most needs. Gaps: the audit buffer is asynchronous in the component view (contradicting the synchronous claim), and residency enforcement and data stores are not explicit.
justifications.maintainability: Clear decomposition: separate Stateless Core, Consent Middleware, AI Audit Proxy, adapters, sidecars and observability. Responsibilities are distinct with low coupling. Minor issues: combined US/EU adapter container, an overloaded core service, and a Telemetry Exporter that is partly redundant.
justifications.portability: Containerized microservices, Envoy, OpenTelemetry and MQTT are portable, and the two GCP regions are targeted. But GCP Secret Manager, KMS and Persistent Disk create lock-in, and there are no IaC, regional deployment or Kubernetes definitions.

elements: Video Streaming Gateway Containers with Local Storage/Caching Agents
sensitivity_points: No autoscaling or capacity mechanism for TURN/STUN and media routing
tradeoffs: Store-and-forward caching adds I/O overhead versus join latency
PERF-01.justification: WebRTC gateway exists, but nothing addresses scaling to 5,000 concurrent sessions or join-time targets. No autoscaling, SFU or load distribution is described. Join under 10 s is unsupported.

sensitivity_points: Synchronous audit logging sits in the latency path
External AI service capacity unspecified; no scaling or caching
tradeoffs: Synchronous traceability logging versus 3 s p95 latency
PERF-02.justification: A gRPC inference proxy exists, but the AI service is external with no stated capacity or autoscaling for about 14 requests/s. Synchronous logging adds latency. The 3 s p95 target is unsupported by any mechanism.

elements: Video Streaming Gateway Containers with Local Storage/Caching Agents
Local Async Event Bus / Queue Containers
sensitivity_points: Cache and queue are server-side, not on client device
tradeoffs: Local buffering improves resilience but delays data sync and adds PHI storage risk
AVAIL-01.justification: Adaptive bitrate WebRTC and store-and-forward address low bandwidth. But caches sit on server containers, not client devices. Clinical note preservation and session reconnection are unspecified, so no-loss guarantees are unproven.

elements: Regional Audit and Compliance Logging Subsystem
sensitivity_points: No disaster recovery or in-region failover for us-central1
tradeoffs: Strict residency prevents failover to EU, limiting redundancy options
AVAIL-02.justification: Regional stacks and a traffic director exist, and residency is respected by not moving data to the EU. But no multi-zone deployment, backup, replication or recovery procedure is described for a 1-hour restoration.

elements: FHIR Translation Adapter Container (US) and National E-Prescription Adapter Container (EU)
sensitivity_points: One EU module may cover all countries
tradeoffs: Adapter isolation versus a shared container coupling deployment
MOD-01.justification: Separate US and EU adapter modules isolate standards from core logic, supporting changes confined to an adapter. However, a single EU module for all countries and no explicit adapter interface or per-country plugin mean some risk.

sensitivity_points: Model versioning and rollback mechanism not described
Audit buffer is asynchronous, contradicting the synchronous logging claim
tradeoffs: Async buffered audit improves latency but risks traceability gaps
MOD-02.justification: Proxy logs inputs, model version and outputs, and decouples the model service. But there is no model registry, version routing or rollback mechanism. The async audit buffer in the component view conflicts with the synchronous container description.

elements: Regional Audit and Compliance Logging Subsystem
sensitivity_points: Consent store lives in an external provider with unspecified residency
Cross-region request routing and denial logging not explicit
tradeoffs: Default-deny strictness versus clinician access in emergencies
SEC-01.justification: Default-deny ExtAuthz with consent and residency headers is a strong mechanism. But no cross-region data path or denial logging is modeled, and the consent provider's location is unspecified. Enforcement is plausible but incomplete.

sensitivity_points: No propagation of consent revocation to downstream sharing or caches
tradeoffs: Real-time consent checks add latency versus eventual propagation
SEC-02.justification: Per-request consent checks could stop sharing quickly, but no research-sharing flow, revocation propagation, cache invalidation or verifiable evidence of the 24-hour stop is modeled. Purpose-based consent is only implied via headers.
